visual_prior_specs.name: remote_ssh_connection_model
visual_prior_specs.content_description: Documentation diagram showing the local VS Code client, SSH tunnel, remote VS Code Server, remote extensions, and resources on the remote machine.
visual_prior_specs.visual_rationale: This source image efficiently communicates the spatial relationship between local UI/extensions and remote server/workspace execution, which is harder to convey tersely in prose.
visual_encodings: Orange extension blocks distinguish extension placement
Green blocks/cylinder indicate remote resources and processes
text_exclusions: Exact command names and menu paths
forbidden_elements: Redrawn annotations over the source image
Long captions embedded inside the image
Additional logos or branding beyond the source frame

visual_prior_specs.name: ssh_host_entry_prompt
visual_prior_specs.content_description: Documentation screenshot of the VS Code prompt for selecting a configured SSH host or entering a user@host string.
visual_prior_specs.visual_rationale: This source image clarifies the exact prompt style, input slot, and selection affordance for entering or choosing an SSH host, which is a GUI convention prone to ambiguity.
visual_encodings: Highlighted list item = selectable host result
Secondary option = SSH host configuration path
text_exclusions: What hostname to use in the user's own environment
Any prose explanation of when to choose enter versus select
forbidden_elements: Synthetic hostnames presented as actual user values
Extra arrows or highlights not present in source unless explicitly added outside the reused image

visual_prior_specs.name: remote_platform_selection_dialog
visual_prior_specs.content_description: Documentation screenshot of the VS Code dialog asking for the remote host platform, with Linux, Windows, and macOS options.
visual_prior_specs.visual_rationale: This source image resolves the UI ambiguity of the remote OS selection step by showing the actual dialog layout and available platform choices.
visual_encodings: Dialog title = remote host platform prompt
text_exclusions: How to determine the user's server OS
Consequences of choosing the wrong OS
forbidden_elements: Task-instance specific server names framed as required values

visual_prior_specs.name: remote_ssh_setting_example
visual_prior_specs.content_description: Documentation screenshot of a Remote.SSH setting entry in VS Code settings, illustrating where an advanced SSH-related option appears.
visual_prior_specs.visual_rationale: This source image helps users recognize the settings UI location and formatting for Remote.SSH options, which prose alone may not anchor clearly.
visual_encodings: Setting title row = identifiable settings entry
Description text block = advanced setting context
text_exclusions: Whether the setting should be enabled for a specific environment
forbidden_elements: Claiming this setting is always required

image_roles: Conceptual model image for explaining local-versus-remote behavior before action steps
UI prompt image for the SSH host entry/selection step
UI dialog image for the remote platform selection step
Settings screenshot for optional advanced configuration reference
binding_protocol.coordinate_system: Source-frame indexing only; each reused image is referenced by its source_frame_index and bound to a prose step, not by screen coordinates.
text_to_visual_binding: When text explains where code, terminals, and extensions run, reference remote_ssh_connection_model.
When text instructs the user to choose or type an SSH destination, reference ssh_host_entry_prompt.
When text instructs the user to identify the remote OS, reference remote_platform_selection_dialog.
When text mentions optional Remote.SSH settings, reference remote_ssh_setting_example.
In operational guidance, each reused image should be referenced only when it clarifies the current step or next action.
task_binding_rules: Bind images only to the procedural steps they directly support; do not include unrelated extracted frames.
Treat all literal hostnames, machine names, and highlighted selections in source images as examples, not as mandatory inputs.

Keep the workflow structure ordered: prerequisites -> install/open Remote-SSH -> enter/select host -> choose platform if prompted -> open remote folder/workspace -> optional settings/troubleshooting context.
If a step has no useful extracted image, keep that step as text guidance rather than inventing a new visual reference.
anti_leakage_rules: Do not output private file paths, benchmark coordinates, or synthetic click locations.
Do not fabricate unseen UI elements beyond what the source frames show.
Do not convert example hostnames from the screenshots into user-specific answers.
Do not embed long instructional prose into image assets; keep explanations in text.

runtime_protocol.update_rule: Inspect the current user context or GUI state, infer the Remote-SSH stage, bind the relevant source image to that stage, and advance one concrete action at a time.
runtime_protocol.stop_condition: Stop when VS Code is connected to the remote host and the user can open or edit a remote folder/workspace, or when missing user input blocks progress.

usage_constraints: Reuse source documentation images instead of generating new priors because the extracted frames already contain relevant UI examples.
This skill is for operational Remote-SSH guidance, not for solving environment-specific SSH authentication problems.
Avoid introducing unsupported UI paths that are not reflected in the provided material summary or source frames.
Keep images as step-bound visual references and prose as the carrier of actionable instructions.
Do not include benchmark answers, coordinates, or hidden environment details.
